newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices off 1/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices off 1/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were off about 1/8 of a point early Wednesday, as a number of bond deals hit the market. A total of $1.1 billion of issues are expected to be priced today.
"There is not a lot of trading," said one bond trader. "People are assessing the market."
In morning trade, the government long bond was up 1/32 at 98-25/32 to yield 6.72 percent.
On Tuesday, muni bonds lost 1/8 to 1/4 point after a large slate of new issue pricings, bid-wanted lists in the secondary, and a downturn in the Treasury market.

September municipal futures were off 6/32 early Wednesday to 117-26/32, while September Treasury futures were off 4/32 to 111-24/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts was 194, down one tick from the Tuesday close of 196 ticks.

In the short-term market on Wednesday, Merrill Lynch & Co. said it priced $1.3 billion of Los Angeles County, Calif., tax and revenue anticipation notes (TRANs) with a 3.80 percent yield and a 4.50 percent coupon. The notes are dated 7/1/1997 and due 6/30/1998.
Wednesday's new bond deals are expected to total $1.1 billion in 39 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $605 million in 14 sales, with a $133 million Sacramento Municipal Utility District, Calif., deal through Goldman, Sachs & Co. topping the list.
Goldman tentatively priced the offering with a top yield of 5.40 percent in 2024.
Elsewhere, $133 million of Michigan Municipal Bond Authority bonds were priced with a top yield of 5.48 percent in 2020.
On the competitive side, 25 sales totaling $496 million are scheduled. A $200 million Massachuesetts Bay Transportation Authority deal at 1300 EDT is the largest.
